parts.ask: Why does the big gear turn slower but stronger?

explain.say: The push at the teeth is the same on both gears, but the big gear's teeth are three times further from its centre. So it turns three times slower, with about three times the turning force, called torque.

explain.say: The gear ratio here is 30 divided by 10, which is 3 to 1. Swap the gears round and a big gear driving a small one gives more speed but less force.

faq.a: A gear ratio compares the teeth on the driven gear with the teeth on the driver gear. A 10-tooth gear turning a 30-tooth gear gives 3 to 1: the driver turns three times for every one turn of the driven gear.
asks: How do you work out a gear ratio?
What does 3 to 1 mean for gears?

faq.q: What does the driver gear do?
faq.a: The driver gear is the one turned by the motor or your hand. Its teeth push on the teeth of the next gear and pass the turning motion along.

faq.q: Why does the big gear turn slower but stronger?
faq.a: The big gear needs more teeth to pass before it completes a turn, so it turns slower. Its teeth are further from its centre, so the same push gives a bigger turning force.
asks: Why do big gears have more force?
Why is the big gear slower?

faq.q: Which way do meshing gears turn?
faq.a: Two gears that mesh always turn in opposite directions: if the driver turns clockwise, the driven gear turns anticlockwise.
asks: Do two gears turn the same way?

faq.q: Do gears give you free energy?
faq.a: No. Gears trade speed for force or force for speed, but the energy out is never more than the energy in. A little is always lost as heat and sound through friction between the teeth.

facts: Two meshing gears always turn in opposite directions.
A gear ratio is the number of teeth on the driven gear divided by the number on the driver gear.
The ancient Greek Antikythera mechanism, over 2,000 years old, contains about 30 bronze gears.

quiz.say: A 12-tooth gear drives a 36-tooth gear. How many turns of the small gear make one turn of the big gear?
quiz.show: A 12-tooth gear drives a 36-tooth gear. How many turns of the small gear make one turn of the big gear?
quiz.why: 36 divided by 12 is 3, so the small gear turns three times for each turn of the big gear.

wrong.0: Only gears with the same number of teeth turn once each.
wrong.2: Twelve is the number of teeth on the small gear, not the number of turns.
